summary: Arrancar matches the blueprint, is wired at main.go:115, and the new tests kill both the missing-gate and naked-one-shot-connect mutants; contract-check clean, all gates green.
missing_tests: The single wiring line (main.go:115 'go supervisor.Arrancar(ctx, sesion.EstaEmparejada())') has no automated coverage: package main reports 'no test files'. This is the exact bug family the task fixes (built but not wired), so the wiring itself is verified only by code reading and by the pending lab restart rehearsal. Accepted because the project has no main-package test harness and adding one is out of contract scope.
notes: contract-check ok=true; violations: none; not_checked: forbid.behaviors. acceptance-coverage status=pass, gaps: none, AC-1..AC-5 all covered.

Manually audited every forbid.behaviors entry (the one item contract-check cannot evaluate): reintentarConexion, procesarEvento, procesarDesconexion, entrarEnPausaTerminal, enPausa, tomarPolitica, soltarPolitica, emitirEstado, esperarBaneoTemporal, intervaloDeRetroceso, intervaloNormal and intervaloBaneo are byte-identical to base; no new Supervisor struct field; taxonomia.go, emparejamiento.go, servidor/*.go, ipc/mensajes.go, go.mod, go.sum and all Rust files untouched; no new ipc.Causa constant; Arrancar does not import or reference canal.Sesion (it gates only on the caller-supplied bool, preserving the existing decoupling); main.go calls it in a goroutine, not synchronously. All 15 behavior clauses satisfied.

DESIGN CONFORMANCE: Arrancar is a 9-line gate plus a direct call into the unmodified reintentarConexion with a new log-detail-only cause constant 'arranque_inicial'. The initial connect therefore inherits the full backoff, terminal-pause and single-flight discipline, including the IntervaloInicial wait before the first dial, exactly as blueprint step 1 and spec design point 1 require. The empty-store invariant holds structurally: !emparejada returns before any connect, so pairing remains the only entry to a first connection.

WIRING VERIFIED: exactly one caller, main.go:115, placed immediately after sesion.RegistrarManejador(supervisor) and roughly 30 lines BEFORE srv.Escuchar/srv.Aceptar, so the startup connect is independent of and prior to any IPC client attaching. sesion.EstaEmparejada() is evaluated synchronously in the main goroutine at the 'go' statement (Go argument-evaluation order), so the gate value is deterministic at startup and cannot drift.

TEST DISCRIMINATION (LES-036) PROVEN BY MUTATION, not by reasoning alone. Pre-fix tree: Supervisor.Arrancar does not exist, so all three tests fail to compile - they cannot pass against pre-fix code. Mutant M1 (emparejada gate removed, always connect): TestSupervisorArrancarSinDispositivoEsNoOp FAILS. Mutant M2 (naked one-shot s.conectar(ctx) + emitirEstado instead of the retry loop, the most plausible wrong fix): TestSupervisorArrancarConDispositivoEmparejadoDisparaConexionYEmiteEstadoActiva and TestSupervisorArrancarConFallosReintentaSegunRetroceso both FAIL on 'esperas = [], se esperaba [1s]' and '[1s 2s 4s]'. The tests assert distinctive postconditions (exact backoff sequence, connect-call count, single 'activa' emission, 'causa=arranque_inicial' in the log, and total log silence on the no-op path), not merely absence of error.

CONCURRENCY: the three new tests call Arrancar synchronously on the test goroutine, so the closure counters they mutate are not shared across goroutines despite t.Parallel(); go test -race -count=1 over the whole sidecar module is clean (independently re-run by this review, all 7 packages ok).

PAIRING RACE (AC-3) holds without new locking, as the blueprint claims: Arrancar only dials when EstaEmparejada()==true, while IniciarEmparejamientoQr and SolicitarCodigoDeVinculacion both return ErrYaEmparejada before reaching Conectar under that same condition. The two are mutually exclusive for the life of one process, so an orden_emparejar arriving while the startup connect is in flight or already connected is rejected by the existing guard, which remains the authority. An overlapping disconnection event during the startup connect is absorbed by the pre-existing single-flight reservation (tomarPolitica) and logged as canal.politica_en_curso; no double-connect window was found.

RESIDUAL RISK 1 (for the human gate, most likely to be misread during the lab rehearsal): on a successful startup connect the Supervisor emits EstadoActiva through srv.EnviarEstadoSesion, but at that moment the IPC server has usually not accepted a nucleo connection yet (Escuchar/Aceptar run later in main), and EnviarEstadoSesion drops the message when s.actual is nil. Supervisor.ultimoEstado is written but read nowhere in the sidecar, so there is no state replay on a later nucleo connect. The cell will be genuinely connected and functional, and the sidecar log will show it (which is what AC-1 makes observable), but the nucleo may never receive an 'activa' estado_sesion until the next disconnection event. This is pre-existing behavior newly reachable at startup, violates no acceptance criterion, and matches the spec's own 'remaining lab-findings queue' non-goal; recommended as a separate micro-task rather than a change here.

RESIDUAL RISK 2: main.go passes context.Background(), which is never cancelled, and the Arrancar goroutine is not awaited at SIGTERM. There is no goroutine leak in practice because the process exits immediately after sesion.Cerrar(), but a narrow window exists in which a retrying startup connect could re-dial just after the ordered shutdown disconnected the client. The blueprint declared this out of scope ('no new ctx derivation, no new cancellation wiring'), and the contract forbids adding it, so the implementation conforms; recording it as declared debt, not a defect of this diff.

RESIDUAL RISK 3, minor documentation regression: the canal.go Conectar comment edit (5 added / 4 removed) replaced rather than extended the prior honesty paragraph, dropping the HEX-026 disclosure that the package tests exercise only the connect-failure path via an explicitly cancelled context, and the new sentence 'los tests de este paquete ejercitan unicamente el cableado de Arrancar' now understates what the package actually covers. Blueprint step 3 asked not to restructure the rest of the comment. Overall honesty is preserved and arguably sharpened (it names the pending network-cut rehearsal as the only real-channel proof and claims no real-channel validation), so this is not blocking; worth folding into the next touch of this file.

VALIDATION HONESTY: 05-validation.json records command 8 as 'cd sidecar && go test -race -count=1 ./internal/canal/...', dropping the trailing './...' the contract specifies. This review independently ran 'go test -race -count=1 ./...' over the whole module and it passed (all 7 packages ok), so the substance of the contract command is satisfied and no coverage gap exists; only the recorded command string is inexact.

adr-0019 / adr-0010: the only new log content is the literal 'arranque_inicial' carried in an existing Detalle field. No QR payload, phone number or JID appears in any added line. Protocol untouched: no new IPC message type or field, wire version 4 and the closed set of 11 types intact, estado_sesion semantics unchanged (the cause string never reaches an ipc.EstadoSesion; reintentarConexion uses it only in log details). No dependency change and no whatsmeow re-pin.

STATUS.md: one bullet appended as the LAST entry of the Definido section, immediately before '## Pendiente' - correct position per file convention, and the placement error made in HEX-026 is not repeated. No existing bullet, including the adjacent HEX-026 entry, was edited or deleted (6 insertions, 0 deletions).

REGRESSION: reconexion_interno_test.go is purely additive (118 insertions, 0 deletions); canal_test.go, emparejamiento_test.go and taxonomia_interno_test.go are untouched. Full module suite green with -race, so the HEX-026 pairing paths and the existing Supervisor state-machine tests are unchanged and passing.

SPEC-VS-CODE MISMATCH confirmed and correctly handled: 00-spec.yaml's root cause claims the supervisor 'is never referenced again anywhere', but sesion.RegistrarManejador(supervisor) has forwarded raw events to procesarEvento since commit 5906778. AC-2's event-routing half was therefore already satisfied by existing code and needed no change; only AC-1's missing initial-connect entry point was the real gap, and fixing it resolves the observed deadlock because no whatsmeow event can fire before a first successful connect. The blueprint flagged this for human confirmation and the diff correctly changed no event-routing code.
